extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators (researchers) applying to ERC Starting, Consolidator, Advanced and Proof of Concept grants; host institutions and research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, eligibility, evaluation criteria and procedural requirements for applying to European Research Council (ERC) frontier research grants (Starting, Consolidator, Advanced) under the 2015 Work Programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence is the sole criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific excellence is the sole criterion on the basis of which ERC frontier research grants are awarded. The evaluation is conducted by peer review panels of renowned scientists and may be assisted by remote experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation designed to identify excellence irrespective of gender, age, nationality or institution; takes career breaks and unconventional career paths into account; evaluations are monitored for transparency, fairness and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion — Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the objectives of the proposed project consistent with the requirements specified in the work programme and/or call for proposals? Do they, where appropriate, correspond to, or go beyond, best current practice?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked on a scale of 0 to 5 as part of the peer review evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion — Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the project have a substantial impact in the context of the ERC objectives?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked on a scale of 0 to 5; used to assess the project's potential to advance frontiers of knowledge and set inspirational targets for research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion — Quality and efficiency of the implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the proposed methodology and work plan effective in reaching the goals of the project? Do they ensure the highest quality and/or utility of results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked on a scale of 0 to 5; panels assess methodology, workplan, feasibility and resource allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring and threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Each evaluation criterion is scored 0–5 and an overall quality threshold of 80% is used to establish the retained list of proposals which will be ranked for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels combine criterion scores to decide retained list; threshold applied to overall evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding justification and panel assessment of budget
rubrics_metrics.description: The funding requested must be fully justified by an estimation of the real project cost. During peer review, panels will assess the funding requested against the needs of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels may suggest modifications to the indicative budgetary breakdown where requests are not properly justified and shall explain such suggested modifications in writing; PI may modify budgetary breakdown during the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union contribution / eligible costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Union financial contribution will reimburse up to 100% of total eligible and approved direct costs and a flat-rate financing of indirect costs of 25% of total eligible direct costs (with exclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions include direct costs for subcontracting and costs of resources provided by third parties not used on host institution premises; final paid amount must be justified on costs actually incurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal completeness and scope eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals must be complete and submitted before the relevant call deadline; a complete proposal entails all parts or sections. The content must relate to the objectives and to the grant type set out in the call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete proposals may be declared ineligible. Scope-based ineligibility is declared only in clear-cut cases. If eligibility is in doubt, evaluation may proceed pending an eligibility review committee decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible scientific fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be made in any field of research; ERC operates on a 'bottom-up' basis without predetermined priorities and encourages interdisciplinary and pioneering proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals within Annex I to the Euratom Treaty (nuclear energy applications) should be submitted under Euratom calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Principal Investigator — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators (PIs) of any age and nationality may apply and may reside anywhere at time of application, but must intend to conduct research in an EU Member State or Associated Country and meet grant-specific eligibility (PhD-date based streaming).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs funded shall spend a minimum percentage of total working time in an EU Member State or Associated Country and a minimum percentage on the ERC project (see grant-specific profiles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Principal Investigator — PhD award windows / streaming
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific eligibility criteria based on date of award of first PhD (or equivalent) apply: Starting Grants — awarded first PhD ≥2 and ≤7 years prior to 1 Jan 2015; Consolidator Grants — >7 and ≤12 years prior to 1 Jan 2015; Advanced Grants — no PhD-age restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective elapsed time can be reduced for documented circumstances (maternity/paternity, long-term illness, clinical training, national service) with specified reductions; reference date is date of actual award according to national rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time commitment minima for Starting Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators funded through ERC Starting Grants shall spend a minimum of 50% of their total working time in an EU Member State or Associated Country and a minimum of 50% of their total working time on the ERC project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time commitment will be monitored; insufficient actual commitment may lead to measures including reduction, suspension or termination of the grant per the grant agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time commitment minima for Consolidator Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators funded through ERC Consolidator Grants shall spend a minimum of 50% of their total working time in an EU Member State or Associated Country and a minimum of 40% of their total working time on the ERC project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As above, time commitment monitored and may trigger corrective measures if below minima or below levels indicated in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution eligibility and commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institution (Applicant Legal Entity) must engage the Principal Investigator for at least the duration of the project and must be established in an EU Member State or Associated Country (or certain eligible international EU organisations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host must provide appropriate conditions enabling the PI to: apply for funding independently; manage research and funding and make resource allocation decisions; publish independently as senior author; supervise team members; and have access to appropriate space and facilities. Host institutions (public or private) must not constrain PI by entity research strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution primary responsibility for research integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Host institutions have the primary responsibility for detection, investigation and adjudication of scientific misconduct arising during evaluation or project life-cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institutions expected to have structures in place to verify no pending allegations against applicants and to inform the ERC of any such allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portability of ERC grants
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grants are portable as described in the ERC Model Grant Agreement: the PI may request transfer of the entire grant or part of it to a new beneficiary under specific conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions may include transfer of equipment purchased and used exclusively for implementation of the project; portability provisions are subject to supplementary agreements between the PI and host institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiaries of ERC grants must ensure open access to all peer-reviewed scientific publications relating to the project results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed requirements are in the Horizon 2020 ERC Model Grant Agreement. Beneficiaries may optionally opt-in individually to the Horizon 2020 Pilot on Open Research Data, which carries additional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed research activities shall comply with ethical principles and relevant national, Union and international legislation (including Charter of Fundamental Rights and ECHR). Particular attention to proportionality, privacy, protection of personal data, physical/mental integrity, non-discrimination and human health protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research must have exclusive focus on civil applications. Funding for human embryonic stem cell research is possible only within Horizon 2020 ethical framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research integrity and sanctions for misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases of scientific misconduct (fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, misrepresentation) arising during evaluation or project life-cycle will be addressed vigorously and may lead to sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions may include exclusion of proposals from evaluation, requests for measures by host institution, reduction of the grant, suspension or termination of grants; ERC evaluation process also governed by rules on confidentiality and conflict of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on submission (limits on re-submission and participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve evaluation quality, restrictions apply: only the first eligible proposal by a PI in a Work Programme is evaluated; PIs with category C in 2014 Starting/Consolidator/Advanced cannot submit to 2015 or 2016; PIs with category B in 2014 cannot submit to 2015; a researcher may participate as PI or Co-Investigator in only one ERC frontier research project at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PI who is participating as PI in an ERC frontier research project may not submit another proposal unless the existing project ends no more than two years after the call deadline. Serving Panel Members for a 2015 ERC call or who served in 2013 may not apply to a 2015 call for same grant type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting Grant — objectives and profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting Grants support PIs starting their independent research team/programme; applicants must demonstrate ground‑breaking nature, ambition and feasibility of proposal and potential for research independence and maturity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum award up to EUR 1,500,000 for 5 years (plus up to EUR 500,000 for specified start-up/major equipment/large facilities). Competitive applicants should show at least one important publication without their PhD supervisor and a promising track record appropriate to field and career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting Grant — early achievements track record
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Track Record applicants should list up to five publications in major international peer‑reviewed journals (highlight those without PhD supervisor as co-author) and number of citations; research monographs, granted patents, invited presentations, prizes/awards/academy memberships (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This evidence supports demonstration of potential for independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidator Grant — objectives and profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidator Grants support PIs consolidating their independent research team/programme; applicants must demonstrate ground‑breaking nature, ambition and feasibility and evidence of research independence and maturity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum award up to EUR 2,000,000 for 5 years (plus up to EUR 750,000 for specified start-up/major equipment/large facilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidator Grant — early achievements track record
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Track Record applicants should list up to ten publications in major international peer‑reviewed journals (highlight those without PhD supervisor as co-author) and number of citations; research monographs, granted patents, invited presentations, prizes/awards/academy memberships (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates research independence and maturity appropriate to career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grant — objectives and profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced Grants support established research leaders with a recognised track record of research achievements; applicants must demonstrate ground‑breaking nature, ambition and feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum award up to EUR 2,500,000 for 5 years (plus up to EUR 1,000,000 for specified start-up/major equipment/large facilities). There is little prospect of success without a track record of significant research achievements in the last 10 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grant — ten-year track record benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced applicants are expected to demonstrate significant achievements in the last 10 years; indicative benchmarks include 10 publications as senior author in major journals, or 3 major research monographs (with translation), or alternative benchmarks such as 5 granted patents, 10 invited presentations, organising major conferences, leadership in innovation, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Track Record applicants should list up to ten representative publications from the last ten years (main author) and may include monographs, patents, invited presentations, expeditions led, organisation roles, prizes/awards, mentoring contributions, and examples of leadership in industrial innovation or design. Consideration can be extended for documented maternity/paternity/long-term illness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension/reduction of eligibility/track-record periods for career breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective elapsed time since PhD award or the ten‑year track record period can be reduced/extended for properly documented circumstances: maternity (18 months per child), paternity (documented leave taken), long-term illness (documented leave over 90 days), clinical training or national service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must properly document circumstances; rules differ for computation of eligibility windows and track-record extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible host institution — additional team members and non-EU entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institution is expected to be the only participating legal entity, but additional team members may be hosted by additional legal entities (eligible for funding) where they bring scientific added value; those entities may be established anywhere (including outside EU/Associated Countries) and are eligible if their participation is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Annex 3 for Associated Countries and restrictions; consortia agreements are not required for ERC multi-beneficiary grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field work outside EU permissible when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: It is expected that the research project will be implemented within Member States or Associated Countries, but this does not exclude field work or other research activities outside the EU/Associated Countries when necessary to achieve scientific objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such activities should be justified as necessary for achieving the scientific objectives of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel structure and subject classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are allocated to ERC panels covering Physical Sciences & Engineering, Life Sciences and Social Sciences & Humanities with detailed panel codes (PE1–PE10, LS1–LS9, SH1–SH6) describing specific subfields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should select/justify the appropriate panel; panels are used to organise peer review and allocate indicative budgets by panel demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial support to third parties — required proposal elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proposal foresees financial support to third parties, it must detail objectives and results and include at least: a closed list of qualifying activities; persons or categories eligible; criteria for awarding support; criteria for calculating exact amounts; maximum amount per third party (may not exceed EUR 60,000 unless necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further boundary conditions may be set in relevant calls. Grant beneficiaries must ensure recipients allow ERC, Commission, European Anti-fraud Office and Court of Auditors to exercise control powers on documents and premises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgetary figures indicative and flexible
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening dates, deadlines and budget amounts are indicative and subject to change; Director-General may open or delay calls within specified windows, and final budgets may vary (up to 20%) following evaluation of proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should treat published budgets and dates as indicative and verify final call texts for definitive amounts and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD equivalence policy
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for Starting or Consolidator Grants a PI must have been awarded a PhD or equivalent doctoral degree; first-professional degrees (even if titled 'Doctor') are not considered equivalent by themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance/references provided (EURYDICE, NSF lists); medical doctors without a PhD must provide both MD and PhD or proof of appointment requiring doctoral equivalency plus research experience (publications). Special rules apply to calculate eligibility time-windows for MD holders.
